issues.description: PaymentDetails interface stores sensitive PCI data (full card number, CVV) in plain text, creating a critical data exposure risk and PCI-DSS compliance violation
issues.suggestion: Never store or log full card numbers or CVVs. Use a payment processor (Stripe, PayPal) that handles PCI compliance. Only store tokenized payment methods: `interface PaymentDetails { paymentToken: string; amount: number; }`

issues.description: SQL query vulnerable to SQL injection - cardNumber is user-controlled and concatenated in slice operation before being used in query
issues.suggestion: While the query itself uses parameterization, ensure cardNumber cannot contain malicious data. Better: never accept raw card data - use payment processor tokens instead

issues.description: Feature access control performed only in application code without server-side enforcement, allowing client-side bypass of premium features
issues.suggestion: This function should be called server-side only. Add middleware to verify subscription status on protected API routes: `app.use('/api/premium/*', async (req, res, next) => { if (!await hasFeatureAccess(req.userId, req.feature)) return res.status(403).json({error: 'Premium required'}); next(); })`

issues.description: Payment processing function accepts payment details directly from client, allowing manipulation of card data, amount, and tier - no server-side validation of pricing
issues.suggestion: Never accept payment details from client. Server should calculate amount based on tier: `export async function processPremiumPayment(userId: string, paymentToken: string, tier: 'premium' | 'enterprise')` then internally calculate the correct amount

issues.description: Payment amount validation compares client-supplied amount against calculated price, but attacker can send correct amount for 'premium' while requesting 'enterprise' tier
issues.suggestion: Remove amount from PaymentDetails. Calculate server-side only: `const amount = calculateSubscriptionPrice(tier);` then charge that exact amount without client input

issues.description: Card validation performs only basic length checks without Luhn algorithm validation, allowing invalid card numbers through
issues.suggestion: Use a proper card validation library or payment processor. Add Luhn check: `function luhnCheck(num: string): boolean { let sum = 0; let isEven = false; for (let i = num.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) { let digit = parseInt(num[i]); if (isEven) digit *= 2; if (digit > 9) digit -= 9; sum += digit; isEven = !isEven; } return sum % 10 === 0; }`

issues.description: Database query results are not validated - assumes rows[0] exists and has expected structure, could crash or leak data if schema changes
issues.suggestion: Validate query results with type guards: `if (rows.length === 0) return false; const row = rows[0]; if (!row.features || !row.valid_until) throw new Error('Invalid subscription data');`

issues.description: JSON.parse on untrusted database data without try/catch - corrupted data causes unhandled exception and potential DoS
issues.suggestion: Wrap JSON.parse in try/catch and validate: `let features: string[]; try { features = JSON.parse(subscription.features); if (!Array.isArray(features)) return false; } catch { return false; }`

issues.description: Payment failures logged with console.error may expose sensitive error details in logs accessible to unauthorized personnel
issues.suggestion: Use structured logging with sensitive data redaction: `logger.error('Payment failed', { userId, lastFour, error: error.message }); // never log full card data or stack traces in production`

issues.description: Date comparison bug - expires cards at the beginning of the expiry month instead of end of month (off-by-one error)
issues.suggestion: Set to last day of expiry month: `const expiryDateObj = new Date(2000 + parseInt(year), parseInt(month), 0); // day 0 = last day of previous month` or better: `new Date(2000 + parseInt(year), parseInt(month)); // first day of next month`

issues.description: Year 2100 bug - assumes 20XX century with hardcoded 2000 offset, will fail for cards expiring in 2100+
issues.suggestion: Use sliding window: `const currentYear = new Date().getFullYear() % 100; const century = parseInt(year) < currentYear - 10 ? 2100 : 2000; const expiryDateObj = new Date(century + parseInt(year), parseInt(month));`

issues.description: parseInt without radix parameter - could parse octal if input has leading zeros
issues.suggestion: Always specify radix: `const expiryDateObj = new Date(2000 + parseInt(year, 10), parseInt(month, 10) - 1);`

issues.description: Database queries execute without indexing guidance - userId lookups in subscriptions table will become slow as users scale
issues.suggestion: Add database migration comment: `// Requires index: CREATE INDEX idx_subscriptions_user_id ON subscriptions(user_id);` and document in schema setup

issues.description: JSON.parse on database features array without validation - corrupted data or schema changes cause runtime crashes
issues.suggestion: Add validation: `let features: string[]; try { const parsed = JSON.parse(row.features); features = Array.isArray(parsed) ? parsed : []; } catch { features = []; }`

issues.description: Validation error thrown without catching payment details being passed - could leak sensitive data in error logs or responses
issues.suggestion: Throw generic errors without echoing input: `throw new Error('Invalid payment details');` is correct, but ensure error handlers don't log the full payment object

issues.description: Card number validation doesn't check for all-zeros, all-nines, or sequential digits that indicate test/fake cards
issues.suggestion: Add basic fraud checks: `if (/^0+$|^9+$|^1234567890123456$/.test(cardNumber)) return false;`

issues.description: Magic numbers for tax rate (8%) and processing fee (2.9%) hardcoded without explanation of jurisdiction or processor
issues.suggestion: Extract to named constants with context: `const TAX_RATE = 0.08; // 8% sales tax (CA); const STRIPE_PROCESSING_FEE = 0.029; // 2.9% + $0.30` or load from config

issues.description: Price calculation doesn't include typical payment processor fixed fee (e.g., Stripe's $0.30), undercharging customers
issues.suggestion: Add fixed fee: `const fee = basePrice * PROCESSING_FEE + 0.30; return parseFloat((basePrice + tax + fee).toFixed(2));`

issues.description: Floating point arithmetic on currency without rounding - could produce values like $10.994999999 leading to payment mismatches
issues.suggestion: Round to cents: `return Math.round((basePrice + tax + fee) * 100) / 100;` or use a money library like dinero.js

issues.description: Subscription valid_until set to exactly 1 year from now without considering timezone or end-of-day, could expire subscriptions mid-day
issues.suggestion: Set to end of day in user's timezone or UTC: `validUntil.setHours(23, 59, 59, 999);` or use date library like date-fns

issues.description: Feature lists duplicated in ternary - premium features repeated in enterprise tier logic, violates DRY principle
issues.suggestion: Extract to constants: `const PREMIUM_FEATURES = ['unlimited_todos', 'priority_support', 'custom_themes']; const ENTERPRISE_FEATURES = [...PREMIUM_FEATURES, 'api_access', 'team_collaboration'];`

issues.description: Database import from './database' is not shown - ensure db connection pooling and proper error handling exists
issues.suggestion: Verify db.query uses connection pooling and parameterized queries. Consider using an ORM like Prisma for type safety

codeQuality.summary: Critical security violations: stores PCI data in plain text, accepts payment details from client allowing price manipulation, implements feature access control client-side only. Multiple SQL injection risks, missing input validation, and business logic flaws. Requires complete redesign of payment flow using proper payment processor.

testCoverage.summary: No tests exist for this file. All 7 exported and internal functions handling critical payment processing, subscription management, and feature access control are completely untested.

suggestions.description: Extract magic numbers (tax rate, processing fee, pricing) to module-level constants for better maintainability and reusability. Currently these business rules are buried in function logic.
suggestions.benefits: Constants are discoverable, reusable, and easier to update. Tax rates and fees can be referenced elsewhere. The 'as const' provides stronger type safety.

suggestions.description: Extract feature lists to a typed constant mapping. This removes duplication with hasFeatureAccess logic and makes features discoverable and maintainable.
suggestions.benefits: Single source of truth for features. Type-safe feature strings. Eliminates duplication and makes it impossible for features to drift across functions.

suggestions.description: Extract individual validation concerns (card number, CVV, expiry date) into separate functions. This improves testability and readability.
suggestions.benefits: Each validation can be tested independently. More descriptive function names make the code self-documenting. Easier to add more validation rules later.

suggestions.description: Use early returns to reduce nesting and improve readability. The current if-chain creates unnecessary indentation.
suggestions.benefits: Flatter structure improves readability. Guard clauses make failure cases explicit upfront. Easier to follow the happy path.

suggestions.description: Extract common database query and row mapping logic into a shared helper function to eliminate duplication.
suggestions.benefits: Eliminates duplication of subscription retrieval logic. hasFeatureAccess can now reuse getUserSubscription. Subscription validity check is extracted and reusable. Easier to maintain and test.

suggestions.description: Extract SQL queries to constants at the top of the file or a separate queries object for better organization and reusability.
suggestions.benefits: SQL queries are discoverable and can be reviewed together. Reduces string duplication. Makes it easier to update queries across the codebase.

suggestions.description: Use method chaining for date manipulation instead of mutation for clearer intent.
suggestions.after: const validUntil = new Date(new Date().setFullYear(new Date().getFullYear() + 1));
suggestions.benefits: More functional style reduces mutation. Clearer that we're creating a new date object.

suggestions.description: Simplify the error handling flow by removing the redundant boolean return when an exception is already thrown for validation failures.
suggestions.benefits: Consistent error handling - all failures throw exceptions. Simpler API (void instead of boolean). Callers don't need to check boolean return value.

suggestions.description: Extract the repeated tier union type to a named type alias to ensure consistency and make it easier to add new tiers.
suggestions.benefits: Type reuse prevents drift. PaidTier type excludes 'free' tier at compile time. Adding new tiers requires updating only one location.

suggestions.description: Use parseInt with explicit radix 10 to avoid potential issues with leading zeros being interpreted as octal.
suggestions.before:
const [month, year] = expiryDate.split('/');
const expiryDateObj = new Date(2000 + parseInt(year), parseInt(month) - 1);
suggestions.after:
const [month, year] = expiryDate.split('/');
const expiryDateObj = new Date(2000 + parseInt(year, 10), parseInt(month, 10) - 1);
suggestions.benefits: Prevents potential bugs from octal interpretation of strings like '08' or '09'. Explicit radix is a best practice.

refactorings.summary: The premium.ts file has significant refactoring opportunities: extract magic numbers and feature lists to constants, reduce duplication between database queries, simplify validation logic through extraction, and improve type safety with reusable type aliases.

recommendations.description: Completely redesign payment flow to never handle raw PCI data. Integrate with a PCI-compliant payment processor (Stripe, PayPal, Braintree) that returns payment tokens. Replace PaymentDetails interface to accept only tokens, never card numbers or CVVs.

Remove client-supplied payment amount from PaymentDetails. Calculate pricing server-side only based on tier to prevent price manipulation attacks where users pay premium price but request enterprise tier.

Ensure hasFeatureAccess is called exclusively server-side with proper middleware enforcement on all premium API routes. Implement server-side authorization checks that cannot be bypassed by client manipulation.

Add comprehensive test suite for all payment processing functions (processPremiumPayment, chargeCard, validatePaymentDetails, calculateSubscriptionPrice) with success paths, error handling, and edge cases. Priority: test invalid payment rejection, insufficient amount rejection, and failed payment rollback.

Create critical test cases for feature access control (hasFeatureAccess) covering: no subscription, expired subscription, feature not in tier, and valid access scenarios. Bugs here directly impact revenue protection.

Add input validation and error handling for all JSON.parse operations on database data (lines 165, 184). Wrap in try/catch blocks with type validation to prevent DoS from corrupted data and ensure graceful degradation.

Fix date comparison bugs in card expiry validation: (1) add explicit radix to parseInt calls, (2) expire cards at end of month not beginning, (3) handle year 2100+ with sliding window instead of hardcoded 2000 offset.

Extract magic numbers (pricing, tax rates, processing fees) and feature lists to module-level typed constants. This makes business rules discoverable, prevents duplication, and ensures consistency across pricing calculations and feature grants.
Eliminate duplication between hasFeatureAccess and getUserSubscription by extracting shared subscription retrieval and validation logic. hasFeatureAccess should reuse getUserSubscription internally.

Fix floating-point arithmetic on currency values (line 107). Round to cents using Math.round((amount * 100) / 100) or use a dedicated money library (dinero.js) to prevent payment mismatches from values like $10.994999999.
